identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log

scan.summary: This is an inspection log for a single Toyota forklift (FL-2, propane-powered, unit BFGU25) at Cascade's Portland warehouse. It documents daily pre-shift inspections for September 2026 against a checklist of safety-critical items (tires, forks, brakes, steering, horn, lights, belt, propane tank security, fire extinguisher, data plate, overhead guard). The log shows all items were inspected each day with mostly pass marks (✓) except one defect noted on Sep 9 (horn not working).
scan.freshness_note: Current as of Sep 17, 2026. This is a live log for September. The document is 8 days old. Continue recording entries as shifts occur.

gaps.title: No evidence of corrective action for Horn defect
gaps.description: The log records 'Horn not working' on Sep 9 at 4,847 hours with an 'X' mark, but shows no entry for when the defect was corrected, reported to management, or when the truck was taken out of service. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) requires defects 'shall be immediately reported and corrected.' The Sep 10 entry shows a checkmark for horn (passing), implying repair occurred, but the log does not document this repair.
gaps.fix: Add a 'Defects Found & Corrected' column or section noting the date/time each defect was found, what corrective action was taken, who authorized the repair, and the date repair was verified as complete. Document whether the truck was pulled from service while awaiting repair.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): 'Defects when found shall be immediately reported and corrected.'

gaps.title: No signature or identity verification for inspectors
gaps.description: The log lists operator initials (M.C., J.R., M.C.) but does not show full names, employee IDs, or signatures for each inspector. OSHA training requirements (29 CFR 1910.178(l)) require operators to be trained and competent. This log does not verify that the people inspecting are trained and authorized to do so.
gaps.fix: Include a key or legend showing full name, employee ID, and certification date for each set of initials used. Alternatively, require full signatures on the log. Maintain a separate roster of trained and certified forklift operators with their training/evaluation dates.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(l): employer must train, evaluate, and certify each operator as competent

gaps.title: No separate record that truck is removed from service when defects found
gaps.description: When a defect is found (as with the horn on Sep 9), the standard requires the truck not be placed in service until repaired. The log does not document whether the truck was actually removed from service, for how long, or when it returned to service after the defect was corrected.
gaps.fix: When an 'X' is marked, add a note in the Notes column stating 'REMOVED FROM SERVICE' and the time/date. Add a follow-up entry when the repair is verified and the truck is cleared to return to service.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): 'shall not be placed in service if the examination shows any condition adversely affecting the safety of the vehicle'

gaps.title: No documentation of operator training/certification
gaps.description: This log is referenced against the training standard (29 CFR 1910.178(l)), which requires the employer to maintain written certification for each operator showing their name, evaluation date, and the evaluator's name. The log does not link to or reference a separate training and certification roster.
gaps.fix: Maintain and reference a separate Operator Certification Log that shows: operator name, date of initial training, date of evaluation, evaluator name, truck type(s) cleared to operate, and date of last refresher training (required every 3 years per 1910.178(l)(4)).
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(l)(1)-(4): training, evaluation, and certification requirements
